in Marine Networks
Minghui Dai , Yuan Wu , Senior Member, IEEE, Liping Qian , Senior Member, IEEE,

Abstract—With the rapid development of marine networks,
there have been growing demands for computation-intensive and
delay-sensitive marine applications and services. However, the
limited underwater energy supply and the acoustic channels result
in the low efficiency for computing tasks and high transmission
delay. In this paper, we investigate the unmanned aerial vehicles
(UAVs)-assisted multi-access computation offloading in marine
networks, with the objective of minimizing the energy consumption
of ocean devices. Specifically, for the underwater segment, we
consider the scenario that multiple underwater sensor nodes
(USNs) covered by the unmanned surface vehicle (USV) upload
their sensing data via non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) for
improving the channel utilization. For the radio frequency
segment, we consider the scenario that multiple UAVs hovering in
the air act as the aerial edge servers for providing computing
services, in which the USV offloads the workloads to UAVs via
frequency division multiple access (FDMA) for avoiding their co-
channel interference, while taking into account that a malicious
node overhears the USV’s offloading transmission. To improve the
computation offloading efficiency, we formulate an optimization
problem for USNs and USV to minimize the total energy
consumption by jointly optimizing the USN’s uploading time,

delay, and high packet loss probability, which reduces the on-
demands services in marine applications [11]. In addition, the
USNs are powered by batteries, which might be quickly
exhausted due to the significant consumption for overcoming

Therefore, it is necessary to design an energy efficient compu-

guarantee the reliable data transmission.
Multi-access computation offloading in ocean environment
is an effective approach to improve the computing efficiency
of ocean devices [12], [13], [14]. Existing works focusing on
oceanic computation offloading can be classified into two cat-
egories. One approach is to directly offload the workloads to
unmanned devices (e.g., unmanned surface vehicles (USVs),
autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs)) [15]. This approach
aims to save the energy consumption of USNs by path plan-
ning to shorten the data transmission distance. Another
approach is to exploit the relay transmission to offload the
workloads to terrestrial nodes (e.g., offshore base stations,
unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs)) [16] for processing
through multi-hop routing schemes, which requires at least
one relay node between USN and terrestrial nodes [17]. This
approach mainly focuses on the relay selection and routing
design to improve the relay performance. Different from these
offloading modes, multi-access computation offloading ena-
bles ocean devices to offload their workloads to multiple edge
nodes in marine networks, which has been expected to effec-
tively enhance the computing efficiency.
Existing works adopt the time division multiple access
(TDMA) and frequency division multiple access (FDMA) for
data transmission between USNs and surface nodes in the
underwater environment, since there is no co-channel interfer-
ence among different acoustic channels [18]. However, the
TDMA requires the strict time sequence for data transmission,
which results in high cost on information exchanges. The
acoustic bandwidth resource utilization in FDMA is low,
which degrades the transmission throughput [19]. The non-
orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) [20], [21], which allows
USNs to reuse the same resource block for data transmission,
has been considered as an efficient approach to improve the
channel efficiency and transmission throughput. In addition,
due to the nature of radio broadcasting in radio frequency seg-
ment, malicious nodes can intentionally eavesdrop the radio
signals and decode the transmission data. Therefore, the state-
of-art solutions for improving the data transmission efficiency
and guaranteeing secrecy provisioning in underwater environ-
ment are still the open issues.
Motivated by the above considerations, in this work, we
investigate the UAV-assisted multi-access computation off-
loading via hybrid NOMA and FDMA in marine networks.
The main contributions of this work can be summarized as
follows.
We propose an energy efficient computation offloading
scheme in marine networks, which consists of two trans-
mission segments, i.e., the underwater acoustic transmis-
sion and the radio frequency transmission. In underwater
acoustic transmission, multiple USNs collect sensing
data for data uploading via NOMA to improve the acous-
tic channel utilization. In radio frequency transmission,
multiple UAVs hovering in the air provide aerial comput-
ing services as the aerial base stations, and USV offloads
partial workloads to UAVs subject to the eavesdropping-
attack from malicious node. We formulate a joint optimi-
zation problem of the USNs’ uploading time, USV’s
computation offloading and offloading time, and the
secrecy provisioning, with the objective of minimizing
the total energy consumption of USNs and USV.
Despite the non-convexity of the formulated joint optimi-
zation problem, we exploit a layered structure to decom-
pose the problem. We divide the optimization problem
into a top-problem for solving the USNs’ uploading time
and a sub-problem for optimizing the USV’s computa-
tion offloading and offloading time, and the secrecy pro-
visioning. Regarding the sub-problem, given the USNs’
uploading time, USV’s offloading time and the secrecy
provisioning, we first solve the optimal computation off-
loading for USV. Then, we propose a two-dimensional
line-searching algorithm to find the optimal USV’s off-
loading time and the secrecy provisioning. Regarding the
top-problem, we adopt the line-searching method to find
the optimal USNs’ uploading time.
We finally provide simulations to evaluate the perfor-
mance of the proposed algorithms. Numerical results
demonstrate that the proposed algorithms can obtain the
minimum energy consumption, and verify the effective-
ness and efficiency of the proposed algorithms in com-
parison with the globally optimal solution by LINGO.
The remainder of this paper is organized as follows.
Section II provides the literature review. Section III presents
the system model and problem formulation. The transforma-
tion of the joint optimization problem is presented in
Section IV. Section V proposes algorithms for solving the
joint optimization problem. Numerical results are shown in
Section VI. Section VII closes this paper with conclusion.

information transmission models, jointly optimizing the tra-

the minimum expected throughput overall ships. In [33], a
cooperative multicast communication scheme for maritime
users relying on joint beamforming optimization and relay
design has been proposed to increase the system throughput.
In [34], an overview of a space-based network for the mari-

evaluate the coverage, throughput and real-time reception
capacity of the presented systems. In [35], Yang et al. studied

we exploit the energy efficient computation offloading via
hybrid NOMA and FDMA in marine networks. Specifically,
we consider two transmission modes, i.e., in underwater
segment, these USNs upload their sensing data to USV via
NOMA; in radio frequency segment, USV aggregates the col-

FDMA. We formulate a joint optimization problem to opti-
mize the transmission time, the offloading workloads and the
secrecy provisioning, with the objective of minimizing the
total energy consumption of USNs and USV.

VII. CONCLUSION
In this paper, we have investigated UAV-assisted multi-
access computation offloading via hybrid NOMA and FDMA
in marine networks. In particular, two transmission segments,
i.e., the underwater acoustic transmission and the radio fre-
quency transmission, were respectively exploited for compu-
tation offloading. In underwater transmission segment, we
considered multiple USNs form the NOMA cluster to upload
data to USV via acoustic channels. In radio frequency transmis-
sion segment, we considered that USV offloads partial work-
loads to UAVs for data processing by taking into account the
overhearing attack from a malicious eavesdropper in marine
environment. To improve the computation offloading effi-
ciency, we have formulated a joint optimization problem of the
USN’s uploading time, USV’s computation offloading, USV’s
offloading time, and the secrecy provisioning to minimize the
total energy consumption of USNs and USV. We have pro-
posed a layered structure to decompose the original problem
into a top-problem and a sub-problem, in which efficient algo-
rithms have been proposed to obtain the optimal solutions.
Finally, we have conducted extensive numerical results to dem-
onstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed algo-
rithms compared with benchmark schemes. For the future
work, we will investigate multi-USNs’ NOMA grouping sce-
nario in underwater environment, in which the coalition formu-
lation of NOMA grouping will be studied.
